SELECT COUNT(*) FROM competency WHERE course_id IS NULL

changeSet.author: krusche
changeSet.comment:
An exercise channel is only created for a course exercise: createExerciseChannel returns without doing anything for an exam exercise. Channels that exist for exam exercises therefore predate that and carry no course. Giving them one would make them show up in the channel list of their course, which asks by course id, so they are removed instead, together with anything written in them.
A channel a tutorial group points at is left alone. That cannot be an exercise channel, and there would be nothing sensible to do with the tutorial group, so the row stays and the constraint is skipped rather than the upgrade taking a decision nobody asked for.

changeSet.author: krusche
changeSet.comment: A channel that belongs to a course exercise, a lecture or an exam belongs to their course, so a channel of one of those kinds stored without a course is one whose course was never filled in. An exam exercise is left out on purpose: it has no course of its own, and a channel on one should not exist in the first place.

changeSet.author: krusche
changeSet.comment: The continuous plagiarism control used to write its plagiarism case post without an author. It now writes it in the name of a course instructor, and the posts it left behind get the same treatment: the instructor of the post's course with the lowest id. A post whose course has no instructor keeps its empty author, and the precondition on the next changeset then leaves the column as it is.
changeSet.sql: UPDATE post SET author_id = ( SELECT MIN(ucr.user_id) FROM user_course_role ucr JOIN exercise e ON e.course_id = ucr.course_id JOIN plagiarism_case pc ON pc.exercise_id = e.id WHERE pc.id = post.plagiarism_case_id AND ucr.course_role = 'INSTRUCTOR' ) WHERE author_id IS NULL AND plagiarism_case_id IS NOT NULL;
